title: Monday Morning Quarterback

paragraphs: Monday night is final, so all of NFL Week 7 is graded. Cowboys at Eagles gets the full treatment, because it was the one game where the whole room had the same two tickets. The other 13 games get the short version: the moment that cashed it or killed it, then the grades. Same rules as always. Every game is graded at the card line, and when a handicapper changed a pick at Lock It Up, the new pick is the one that counts. The college recap has its own Gambler page.

Card line: Cowboys −4.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Eagles +4.5 and the Over 44.5, projecting Eagles 24, Cowboys 23. Final: Cowboys 38, Eagles 21. The Cowboys won by 17, and the teams scored 59 points.

One game, one room, two tickets. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches all had the Eagles +4.5 and the Over 44.5. Follow The Money sat it out. The Eagles +4.5 could lose by four and still cash. The Over needed 45 points. The market total slid to 43.5 by Monday evening, but the tickets were written at 44.5, so that is the number they sweated.

The first quarter was a track meet, which the Over loved. Brandon Aubrey opened it with a 55-yard field goal. Quinnen Williams jumped offside with a neutral zone infraction, and on the next snap Saquon Barkley ran 8 yards for a touchdown. Dak Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb for 9 yards and a 10-7 lead. Then another Dallas flag broke the Eagles' way. On 4th-and-1 at the Philadelphia 44, Tanner McKee fumbled the snap and Williams recovered it, and Williams' own offside flag erased the whole play. Later in the drive, on 3rd-and-7 at the Dallas 9, LT Overton was flagged for roughing the passer on an incompletion. Dameon Pierce scored from 5 yards on the next snap. Eagles 14-10, and the Eagles +4.5 was covering by 8.5.

Then came the flag that saved every Eagles ticket in the second quarter. Tyler Goodson took the ensuing kickoff 91 yards for a touchdown, and a holding flag on Dallas' Justin Barron brought it all back. Instead of a Dallas lead, it was still Eagles 14-10. Dallas then went 81 yards in 14 plays anyway, converting a 4th-and-1 at the Philadelphia 44 on a Javonte Williams run, and Prescott hit George Pickens for a 21-yard touchdown. Before the half, Prescott found Lamb for 30 yards down to the Philadelphia 9 with 19 seconds left. Two incompletions later Aubrey kicked a 27-yarder on the final play of the half. Halftime: Cowboys 20, Eagles 14. The Eagles +4.5 was losing by 1.5, and the Over had 34 and needed 11 more.

The third quarter opened with the drive Eagles bettors will tell their grandkids about: 17 plays, 84 yards and 9:16 off the clock. McKee converted a 4th-and-1 at the Dallas 39 with a 15-yard pass to Makai Lemon. Then, on 3rd-and-goal from the 4, he hit Lemon for the touchdown. Eagles 21-20. The Eagles +4.5 was covering by 5.5, and the Over had 41 and needed four.

Here is the swing of the night. Dallas faced 2nd-and-1 at the Philadelphia 18 with 2:17 left in the third. Prescott lost the ball, and Riq Woolen scooped it up and ran 73 yards for a touchdown. Replay called it an incomplete forward pass and took the whole thing back. That would have put the Eagles up 27-20 before the extra point, with the Eagles +4.5 covering by 11.5. Instead, two snaps later, Prescott hit Lamb for a 16-yard touchdown and then ran in the two-point conversion himself. Cowboys 28-21. The Over cashed right there, with 49 points and more than a quarter to play. The side was still alive, because one Eagles field goal would have put them inside the 4.5.

The fourth quarter took that away, and it started with a flag. Cooper DeJean was called for a 17-yard pass interference on the first snap of the next Dallas drive, Javonte Williams ripped off 34 yards two plays later, and Aubrey made a 24-yarder on 4th-and-5 for a 31-21 lead. Now the Eagles +4.5 needed a touchdown. Philadelphia got to the Dallas 32, and DeMarvion Overshown intercepted McKee at the 30 with 7:55 left. Philadelphia got one more look after a Dallas delay of game on 4th-and-1 forced a punt. Quinnen Williams sacked McKee for a loss of 8, and McKee's 4th-and-9 throw to Hollywood Brown fell incomplete. Javonte Williams finished it with a 2-yard touchdown at 2:21. He ran 25 times for 155 yards. Cowboys 38-21.

The grades. The Eagles +4.5 lost by 12.5, and the Over 44.5 won by 14.5, so every picker who played the game went 0-1 on the side and 1-0 on the total. The Formula and The Cover Writer projected Eagles 24, Cowboys 23, and the Cowboys scored 38. Letdown Watch had the Eagles winning 25-21, and the 21 did show up, for the wrong team. Next Man Up and In The Trenches both picked Dallas to win and took the points anyway. In The Trenches had the Cowboys 26-25, and it was right about the winner and missed the margin by 16 points. Ask any Eagles ticket in the room who wrecked it and you get the same three answers: the replay booth that took back Woolen's return, Overshown's interception and Javonte Williams. Ask who cashed the Over and you get Lamb, Aubrey and Javonte Williams. Follow The Money watched Monday night from the couch and went home with its record intact, which it now calls a strategy.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 44.5, cleared it by 14.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Eagles +4.5, missed by 12.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Bears −3, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Patriots +3 and the Under 50.5, projecting Patriots 24, Bears 22. Final: Bears 30, Patriots 24. The Bears won by 6, and the teams scored 54 points.

The Patriots +3 and the Under 50.5 were both alive at 27-21 with eight minutes left, when Cairo Santos hit the right upright from 53. Santos came back out at 1:34 and made a 58-yarder, which put 51 on the board and beat the Under 50.5 by half a point. Andy Borregales' 47-yarder at 0:37 left New England three points short of a push, and Caleb Williams took a knee.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Patriots +3, missed by 3 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 50.5, went over by 3.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Steelers −3.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Steelers −3.5 and the Over 44.5, projecting Steelers 26, Saints 22. Final: Steelers 16, Saints 10. The Steelers won by 6, and the teams scored 26 points.

The Steelers −3.5 was covering by 2.5 when Daniel Carlson lined up a 52-yarder at 9:32 of the fourth that would have flipped it, and he pushed it wide right. Chris Boswell's 37-yarder at 1:04 came off the board on a Saints offside flag, and Aaron Rodgers knelt it out. The Over 44.5 never had a pulse.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Steelers −3.5, covered by 2.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 44.5, fell short by 18.5 points. Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Saints +3.5, missed by 2.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: 49ers −3.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers −3.5 and the Under 50.5, projecting 49ers 27, Falcons 21. Final: Falcons 29, 49ers 20. The Falcons won by 9, and the teams scored 49 points.

The 49ers −3.5 was still breathing at 26-20 after Brock Purdy's 1-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk at 5:05. Then Kendal Daniels intercepted Purdy at 2:42, and Nick Folk's 31-yarder made it 29-20. The Under 50.5 owes two kickers a fruit basket. Folk hit the upright on one extra point and Eddy Pineiro pushed another wide left, and the game finished one and a half points under. Follow The Money's only call of the week was the Over, and those two kicks sank it.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 50.5, stayed under by 1.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the 49ers −3.5, missed by 12.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 50.5, fell short by 1.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side.

Card line: Browns −1.5, total 38.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Titans +1.5 and the Under 38.5, projecting Browns 19, Titans 18. Final: Browns 27, Titans 24. The Browns won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

The Under 38.5 was dead by 4:34 of the fourth, when Deshaun Watson ran 9 yards for a touchdown. Tony Pollard's 1-yard touchdown with 58 seconds left tied it 24-24 and had four pickers covering the Titans +1.5. With three seconds left, Tennessee jumped offside on the field goal try, and Andre Szmyt hit from 32 on the final play. Letdown Watch, alone on the Browns −1.5, has not stopped talking about it.
Called it: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Over 38.5, cleared it by 12.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Browns −1.5, covered by 1.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Titans +1.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Under 38.5, went over by 12.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Vikings −6.5, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Colts +6.5 and the Over 41.5, projecting Vikings 24, Colts 19. Final: Vikings 16, Colts 10. The Vikings won by 6, and the teams scored 26 points.

The Colts +6.5 was hanging on at 13-10 with 2:02 left when Kyler Murray hit Jordan Addison for 34 yards down to the Indianapolis 2, and a holding flag on Minnesota wiped it out. The Vikings settled for Will Reichard's 52-yarder, won by six, and the Colts +6.5 cashed by half a point. That holding flag was worth a whole week to four pickers. The Over 41.5 never got close, and In The Trenches, alone on the Under, cashed it by 15.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Colts +6.5, covered by 0.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 41.5, stayed under by 15.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 41.5, fell short by 15.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Vikings −6.5, missed by 0.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Jets −4.5, total 39.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins +4.5 and the Over 39.5, projecting Jets 23, Dolphins 19. Final: Dolphins 28, Jets 25. The Dolphins won by 3, and the teams scored 53 points.

Sanders' 33-yard field goal at 8:57 of the fourth made it 21-17 and left the Over 39.5 a point and a half short. Malik Willis hit Caleb Douglas for a 63-yard touchdown at 4:44, which took the total from 38 to 45 in one play and buried the Jets −4.5. The Jets' late touchdown and two-point try made it 28-25, and only the score looked close.

Called it: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Dolphins +4.5, covered by 7.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 39.5, cleared it by 13.5 points.
Missed: The Formula and In The Trenches on the Jets −4.5, missed by 7.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Panthers −3.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers −3.5 and the Over 44.5, projecting Panthers 26, Buccaneers 21. Final: Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13. The Buccaneers won by 30, and the teams scored 56 points.

The Panthers −3.5 was finished in the second quarter. Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown, Zyon McCollum returned a blocked extra point for two points, and it was 33-6 at the half. Sean Tucker's 46-yard touchdown run at 10:21 of the fourth cashed the Over 44.5. Next Man Up, alone on the Buccaneers +3.5, cashed by 33.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 44.5, cleared it by 11.5 points. Next Man Up on the Buccaneers +3.5, covered by 33.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Panthers −3.5, missed by 33.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 44.5, went over by 11.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Ravens −2.5, total 51. The Cover Writer's card had the Ravens −2.5 and the Under 51, projecting Ravens 26, Bengals 23. Final: Bengals 35, Ravens 13. The Bengals won by 22, and the teams scored 48 points.

This was the Lock It Up game. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches left the Bengals +2.5 for the Ravens +3, and four pickers left the Under 51 for the Over 46.5. Baltimore led 13-0 late in the first half. Then Joe Burrow threw touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase. At 7:25 of the fourth Demetrius Knight Jr. intercepted Tyler Huntley, and Drew Sample's 16-yard touchdown at 6:21 made it 48 points, over the 46.5 and under the 51, and nobody scored again. Both totals cashed. Neither Baltimore ticket came close.
Called it: The Cover Writer on the Under 51, stayed under by 3 points. The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 46.5, cleared it by 1.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Ravens −2.5, missed by 24.5 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Ravens +3, missed by 19 points.

Lock It Up check: The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Under 51 to the Over 46.5, and the Under 51 would have stayed under by 3 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Bengals +2.5 to the Ravens +3, and the Bengals +2.5 would have covered by 24.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Texans −9.5, total 43. The Cover Writer's card had the Giants +9.5 and the Over 43, projecting Texans 26, Giants 18. Final: Giants 27, Texans 21 in overtime. The Giants won by 6, and the teams scored 48 points.

The Giants +9.5 never needed the points. Cam Skattebo's 16-yard touchdown run at 8:55 of the fourth put New York up 21-14, and C.J. Stroud tied it with 52 seconds left. Regulation ended 21-21, one point short of the Over 43, so In The Trenches was one overtime stop from cashing the Under. Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run in overtime ended that. The Formula's Lock It Up move to the Giants +10.5 turned a loser into a winner by 16.5.

Called it: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Giants +9.5, covered by 15.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 43, cleared it by 5 points. The Formula on the Giants +10.5, covered by 16.5 points.
Missed: In The Trenches on the Under 43, went over by 5 points.
Lock It Up check: The Formula moved off the Texans −9.5 to the Giants +10.5, and the Texans −9.5 would have missed by 15.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Broncos −4.5, total 43.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Cardinals +4.5 and the Over 43.5, projecting Broncos 24, Cardinals 20. Final: Broncos 30, Cardinals 16. The Broncos won by 14, and the teams scored 46 points.

The Cardinals +4.5 needed a stop late in the third, and J.K. Dobbins' 1-yard touchdown on the last play of the quarter survived a replay review and put Denver up 27-13. Wil Lutz's 31-yarder made it 30-13 and left the Over 43.5 half a point short. Then Chad Ryland made a 41-yarder on 4th-and-17 at 6:21. In The Trenches lost the Under to a field goal on 4th-and-17. Of all the ways.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 43.5, cleared it by 2.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Broncos −4.5, covered by 9.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Cardinals +4.5, missed by 9.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 43.5, went over by 2.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Lions −3, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Packers +3 and the Under 53.5, projecting Lions 26, Packers 25. Final: Lions 20, Packers 17. The Lions won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

DJ Wonnum blocked Trey Smack's 35-yarder with the score tied 17-17 at 3:25. That kick would have cashed the Packers +3. Jared Goff knelt at the Green Bay 4, and Jake Bates kicked a 22-yarder on the final play. Three points, refunds all around. The Under 53.5 was never in danger.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 53.5, stayed under by 16.5 points.
Push: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Packers +3, landed exactly on the number. Letdown Watch on the Lions −3, landed exactly on the number.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Rams −4.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Rams −4.5 and the Over 47.5, projecting Rams 27, Raiders 22. Final: Rams 35, Raiders 21. The Rams won by 14, and the teams scored 56 points.

The Raiders cut it to 28-18 at 13:12 of the fourth, and a failed two-point try left the Over 47.5 a point and a half short. Blake Corum's 4-yard touchdown at 6:34 settled both tickets. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches got their switch right, from the Raiders +4.5 to the Rams −3.5. Next Man Up also moved from the Over 47.5 to the Under 48.5, and it will be hearing about that for a while.

Called it: The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Rams −4.5, covered by 9.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 8.5 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Rams −3.5, covered by 10.5 points.
Missed: Next Man Up on the Under 48.5, went over by 7.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 47.5, went over by 8.5 points.

Lock It Up check: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Raiders +4.5 to the Rams −3.5, and the Raiders +4.5 would have missed by 9.5 points. Next Man Up moved off the Over 47.5 to the Under 48.5, and the Over 47.5 would have cleared it by 8.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Seahawks −2.5, total 42.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chiefs +2.5 and the Over 42.5, projecting Seahawks 23, Chiefs 21. Final: Seahawks 20, Chiefs 3. The Seahawks won by 17, and the teams scored 23 points.

The Chiefs +2.5 needed Kansas City inside two, and it was 13-3 when Harrison Butker missed a 45-yarder wide right at 8:38 of the fourth. Emanuel Wilson's 21-yard touchdown run at 3:47 finished it. Letdown Watch was alone on the Seahawks −2.5, In The Trenches was alone on the Under 42.5, and both won by double digits.
Called it: Letdown Watch on the Seahawks −2.5, covered by 14.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 42.5, stayed under by 19.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Chiefs +2.5, missed by 14.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 42.5, fell short by 19.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: That's all 14 games of NFL Week 7, Monday night included. Here is how everybody finished.

The Cover Writer went 5-8-1 against the spread and 9-5 on totals. Add last week's 4-9 against the spread, and the Cover Writer is 9-17-1 against the spread over two NFL weeks. The totals are paying the rent and the sides are sleeping on the couch. Monday night was the whole week in one game: wrong side, right total.
The Formula went 4-9-1 on sides and 9-5 on totals. The Lock It Up switch to the Giants saved it from 3-10-1, and it has mentioned that more than once.
Next Man Up went 5-8-1 on sides and 9-5 on totals. Its original picks would have gone 10-4 on totals. That one move off the Rams Over cost it a game, and it knows exactly which one.

Letdown Watch went 7-6-1 on sides and 9-5 on totals. It is the only handicapper in the room with a winning week on sides. It went along with everybody else on the Eagles Monday night and lost with everybody else.
Follow The Money had no picks on the side and went 0-1 on totals.
In The Trenches went 3-10-1 on sides and 8-6 on totals. It took the Under alone five times and cashed two of them.

The smack talk is already on the Lock It Up line. Letdown Watch says it will never follow the crowd again. In The Trenches wants the Monday night box score framed, because 25 carries for 155 yards is the kind of night it builds a whole card around, even when it picks the wrong side of it. The Formula and Next Man Up point out that Letdown Watch's winning week is one game over even, and it is acting like it won the Super Bowl. Follow The Money says one bad Over isn't a slump, it's a sample. Week 8 opens with Panthers at Packers on Thursday night, and every one of them wants a fresh card.

look_ahead.closing_sentence: Week 8 opens Thursday night with Panthers at Packers. The refreshed Week 8 cards haven't been posted yet, so there are no new numbers or picks here, and we won't run last week's. The current lines and every handicapper's Week 8 picks go up here as soon as the cards are posted.
